title: A 'forbidden' written where absence has no slot is rejected by the engine, not by the SDK.
why: behavioural spec 'forbidden': the SDK does not check where it was written — a 'forbidden' node belongs in a slot (shape spec §5.1) and the engine rejects a misplaced one with 'interaction-invalid' when the interaction is added. A part's body root is not a slot, so the case is that the DSL accepts the call and the refusal arrives from the engine, carrying its own words. An SDK that refused this itself would be holding a copy of §5.1 that can drift.

interaction.description: a body that is nothing at all
